newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia signs border aid deals with EU.
newsitem.headline: Latvia signs border aid deals with EU.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Thursday signed three agreements with European Union Immigration, Justice and Interior Affairs Commissioner Anita Gradin for aid to improve the Baltic state's border controls.

The amount of funds available under the agreements came to some seven million Ecus plus a share of a 14-million-Ecu grant given to Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia and Poland, Latvia's EU representative office said.
The funds are aimed at improving communications, the efficiency of the Baltic state's border as well as measures to help clean the badly polluted Baltic Sea.

"Gradin said the EU was looking at how order was being brought to the eastern borders of the Baltic states and the development of the problem of refugees in the Baltic region," Shkele's office said after the meeting with Gradin.
As Latvia tries to make its case for European Union entry, border controls are a key focus.
Although huge queues at the border crossings between the three Baltic states are mostly a thing of the past, smuggling is rife and many Latvians say their border officials are corrupt.
The Baltic states are also often targeted by people smuggling illegal immigrants to the West although the border police are trying to make their frontiers less porous.
